Inverness harbour improvements, $15,000.

This vote has
been in the Estimates since 1911. The hon. minister gave me an assurance last year that this amount would be expended this year on the harbour of Inverness. Is he still of the same opinion?
Plans are now being prepared for the work.

I take this opportunity of thanking the minister for his intention to have this money spent. The original intention of this undertaking was that this artificial harbour should be opened up for schooners, and that it should have a depth of about fourteen feet. A good deal of expensive work has been done there already. The town of Inverness has a population of about 4,000 now. There are coal mines there-a very important industry, and there is a splendid fishing bank off the coast. The intention is to develop the fishing industry of the town. Does the specification

call for the carrying out of the original plan or has the plan* been changed?
We are just getting out the plans. The explanation of this item does not appear to be here, but it is to provide piers necessary in the harbour of Inverness.
There is a pier on one side of the harbour now. My understanding is that this appropriation is for building a pier on the opposite side.
Yes.

Is there any provision for dredging between those piers? The minister will understand that this is a beach, an artificial harbour, and that the piers are put there for the purpose of keeping the sand back after the dredging has been done.
As soon as these piers are completed, we intend to undertake the dredging, but we have to have the piers in first. The dredging will be done out of the general appropriation for dredging.
The hon. minister will have the work pushed on as rapidly as possible?
We will do the dredging to meet the requirements as soon as the pier is completed.
Can you tell me what depth of water you are going to have?
I do not know that at the moment. That would be governed entirely by the report of the district engineer in charge.

I trust that the minister will see his way clear to carry out this work and that the plans will not be changed, because a great deal of the work, that has already been done, will have been done in vain if the original plans are not carried out.
Kelly's Cove-extension	to breakwater,

There is a Kelly's cove in my county. I am sorry to say this is not my Kelly's cove" that is getting this vote. People in my constituency think this item refers to their Kelly's cove, but I believe it 'belongs to some one else. I would ask the minister to make some distinction so as to show the county in which this cove is, because there is a very old place called Kelly's cove in my county.	.

This cove is in the county of Yarmouth. If my hon. friend desires it,
we shall extend title to his cove and cal! it McKenzie's Kelly's cove.
Margaree harbour-repairs to breakwater, $4,200.

This appropriation is for repairs to breakwater. I am sorry to tell the minister that this is only a drop in the bucket to put the harbour in a proper condition. Some time ago I informed the minister that this process of destruction of the piers had been going on for the last two years, with the knowledge of the department. No attention was paid to my representations. The result is that the Government will be called upon to spend between $35,000 and $45,000 before this harbour is fit for anything. The piers there cost $68,756, but they are in such a condition that I do not think that $4,000 will begin to make any substantial repairs or make good the destruction that has been wrought. The minister will pardon me if I say that this has been done with the knowledge of his department. For the last two years I have called attention to this matter, and I am sure that Mr. Gallant, who has the patronage of the county, should have done his part also. Besides, the minister has the reports of his own engineers. It would be wise in the public interest to have an item in the Supplementary Estimates to put that harbour in condition that the public property may be preserved. If that is not done, the whole structure from the outer end of the pier will be carried away. It is practically carried away now, so far as tire use of the harbour is concerned.
While I am on my feet, I may refer to another public work, that of Port Hood. I think I may be pardoned for taking up a moment now, as these matters are important, and I do not usually take up much of the time of the House. The wharf at Port Hood has been destroyed, section by section, in much the same way as Margaree Harbour piers. The minister is in possession of reports of the last two years with respect to this wharf. The wharf cost the country $70,000, and of that, I am sure, at least $55,000 of the work done has been carried away, not by one storm, but by a succession of storms. The Government undertook to replace this wharf, and had an appropriation, I think, of $5,000 in the estimates last year. Through some lack of knowledge or experience, the work done last year is displaced now, and I may say practically carried away so far as its usefulness to shipping is concerned. The

wharf now would require at least $25,000 to put it into shape that it could be used for shipping. I would ask the Minister to take this into consideration, and to provide in the supplementaries an appropriation to save what has not already been destroyed.
Going further, I might refer to the work of closing the northern end of Port Hood harbour. I still have a strong faith that the Supplementary Estimates will bring forth an appropriation for the continuation of that work. As the minister knows, it was commenced six years ago. I am informed by some parties that it is the intention of the Government to drop this work entirely. The minister will know, no doubt, that this work is going to cost before it is finished some $100,000-I think that is a fair estimate. The undertaking was consented to by the leader of the present Government (Mr. Borden). I have looked over the debates that took place year after year when this work was undertaken and I find that it was consented to by both sides of the House. That being so, I cannot see how the Government can afford to let the work drop, $159,000 having been already spent. There is even a worse feature resulting from the delay in carrying on this work and that is that the harbour which was a fairly good harbour of shelter is being spoiled by the work done by the Government, narrowing the channel, and thus concentrating the force of the water, the current has been diverted and has been increased and large deposits of sand are being formed inside the harbour until the channel is closed, this condition will continue. The longer the condition is allowed to continue, the worse it will grow and the harbour will be practically spoiled, necessitating a great deal of dredging, more than the country will consent to have done. Gan the minister give me any information with regard to the closing of the northern entrance of the harbour of Port Hood?

As this is a matter for
which there is no item in the Estimates before us, I have not the information with regard to Port Hood at hand, but I shall be glad to look it up that I may answer the hon. gentleman's question, If the circumstances are as stated by the hon. gentleman, if the matter has been looked into at some previous time by my right hon. friend the leader of the Government and he gave the assurance that certain work would be carried out, you can depend upon it that that pledge will be kept. So far as the port of

Margaree is concerned, the amount we have in the Estimates at the present time is for the purpose of improving the conditions in a temporary manner, and in the meantime we are having a survey made to ascertain what is necessary to meet the public requirements with a view to carrying out the work.

The hon. minister misunderstood me. I did not say that the right hon. leader of the Government had promised to carry on this work. I said he had consented to the undertaking of the work when it was undertaken. For that reason, I claim, he is in honour bound to carry on the work.	-

One or two of these
items should be allowed to stand. Many hon. members are absent who desire to discuss these matters.

Of course, the hon. gentleman can have any item stand that he wishes. But I can assure him that if any hon. member on the other side wishes to discuss any item, whether it has been passed or not, he will be at perfect liberty to do so as far as I am concerned.
Spry Bay (Henley's) wharf, $3,000.
What is this for?

The work to be done consists of reconstruction of part of an old wharf, which was block and span. w;th a pile addition. When completed it will be 169 feet long, 20 feet wide, with an ell 25 feet by 20 feet and an average depth of 18 feet. Estimated cost of crib-work, 14,400 cubic feet at 8 cents, $1,224; flooring, $276; pile work, $865; land and road approach, $100; warehouse, $500.
That is new work?
It is a re-vote of $1,600.

I am instructed that
this work is entirely unnecessary, that there are only three people at the most who can be served by it, and that there is already a Government wharf about a mile from this one.

I understand that improvements have been made at different times, for example, in 1909 and in 1910 $1,300 was spent in improvements. The repairs seem to be necessary to keep the wharf in good shape; the wharf must be of some use or the repairs would not have been recommended by the engineer.
What engineer recommended the repairs?
Morrison.
Do you propose spending the money this year?

What is to be
done at Tangier?

This amount, $4,200, is
asked by the district engineer for the construction of an extension to the wharf at Tangier. The proposed work will be one solid crib-work block 25 feet by 50; 30,000 cubic feet of crib-work at 8i cents, $2,550; widening and raising of road approach and contingencies, $1,650. The proposed work is of a public nature and will give additional and better accommodation for vessels loading and unloading. The appropriation for 1913 was $1,200, probable expenditure, 1913, $400; re-vote, $800; new vote, $3,400. The wharf was built originally in 1908-9.
The wharves-'breakwater, $1,500.
I move that this item be struck out. The work is completed.

Motion agreed to.
Windsor-harbour improvements, $25,000.
When will the work at Windsor be done?

The work is of a public nature, and will increase the accommodation for the berthing of vessels, provide more railway accommodation, and more room for piling lumber, etc. The improvement of the harbour is also asked for by resolution of the board of trade of Windsor. A large sum of money has already been spent there.
When do you propose spending the money appropriated by this vote?

Just as soon as we can get at the work.
Mr. iMACILEAN: Did you ask for tenders?
Plans are being prepared, and tenders will be called for as soon as they are completed.
Does that mean next year?

No, this year.
Cardigan

extension and reconstruction of ferry wharf, $10,000.
This is the second or third time that this amount has been voted. Does the minister intend to spend the money this coming summer?

The district engineer states that the proposed work will consist in the re-construction of the present wharf, 315 feet long; construction of extension, 40 feet; pierhead, 70 feet, and guide piers, 90 feet, etc. The contract is already let for this work, and it will be gone on with immediately.
Is the work to be done by tender?
Yes.
Why was the work not proceeded with last year?
What is to be done in Charlottetown harbour?
We have a contract there now for dredging.
Is it the intention to build a dry dock?

No, this is all for
dredging.
I suppose this dredging is being done by tender, not by the Government dredges?
It is being done under contract; tenders were, called.
It is under contract after public tender.
Have you done anything yet with regard to the marine slip?
Not yet.

Is it the intention to
do anything this summer?
We will give the matter attention as soon as we can.
Will you have an item in the Supplementaries for it?

I do not recollect whether there is anything in the Supplementaries or not.

North Lake, boat harbour, $24,000.
This is the second time this has been voted and I would like to know why the work has not been gone on with.

There is $24,000 of revote of last year's appropriation for the construction of two piers at this place. The delay is due to the fact that we could not arrive at an understanding with the owners of the adjoining land. If my hon, friend could help us out we would be glad to have his assistance.
What arrangements does the department desire to make?
We are asking a release as against damages to the surrounding land.

Is it expected that by
opening the harbour the sand may Change its course? This is an outlet from a lake that crosses a sand bar.
To some extent. I do not know whether it would do a certain amount of injury.

I understand that the
Conservative candidate in the last election wished to get the farmers owning the adjoining land to sign a document to the effect that if their land was injured by the construction of this work they would waive all claims against the Government, and that they refused to do so.
That is right.
Is it usual to ask men whose land may be injured by the construction of public works to do that sort of thing?

It is always usual when
they would have the direct benefit they would have in this case from the work.

In all probability it will not be possible to come to terms with these men on the conditions laid down by the department. Would it not be desirable to construct the harbour at some other place nearby where no such land injuries are likely to result?

I do not know that it
would be. I could not give an .answer without having a report from an engineer.
I think there is a report in the department that a boat harbour can be constructed near there, at Long Point, without danger from drifting sands.
Could not my hon. friend convince the farmers that we are not asking too much from them? i

I do not know. If their land is valuable and their farms would be destroyed, I think you are asking them to do too much when you ask them to waive all claim to damages. If I owned land there I certainly would not sign such a document and I do not think it is reasonable to ask them to do so. What is the use of having the vote here if it is not intended to expend the money.
We intend to expend the money if we can get the farmers to grant a relief.

You cannot exipect that.
New Brunswick, Bathurst-harbour improve-merits, $100,000.
In what way does the minister intend to do this work, by contract or by dredges belonging to the department?
By contract.

By a new' contract or
by an extension of the contracts of last year?
An extension of the contracts of last year.

I asked last spring to
have instructions given, either t: the captains of the dredges of the department or to the contractors, to first dredge the sand bars which are on the inside of the harbour over which the water is not so deep as in the general channel. When last summer I saw that they had not done that I called the attention of the chief engineer to it and immediately one of the dredges of the department, the St. Lawrence, went to work on the upper bar. They have done some work there. The lower bar not being dredged, however, there is no more advantage to navigation than if nothing had been done. I understand the contractors made some objections, claiming that the work belonged to them and that they were not ready to do it. I do not care how it is done, but last fall the shippers were greatly handicapped by the want of facilities. Two or three more ships could have been brought up in the late season and could have been loaded; whereas, owing to the condition of the bar, the lumber had to be kept in until spring. I would urge the minister to see that

the inside bars are dredged at once to the
level of the harbour. That could he done in a week's work. A great deal of correspondence has taken place with the department about the deposit of the spoil of the dredges into Bathurst channel. Everybody in Bathurst and Gloucester county knows that I want every inch of water possible for the main channel and when I objected to the affluent into that channel it was because it would not help navigation at all. A breastwork should be put in at the point of divergence and nobody knows that better than the chief engineer for he made a survey of that harbour twenty years ago, and conditions have not changed since. I see that the resident engineer recommends that a training wall should be built near the old mill, called at that time the Bathurst mill. He says it could be done for about $4,000 and it is certainly the only practical way of reserving the water for the main channel. I wish to impress upon the minister the necessity of having that work done.
Do I understand that my hon. friend considers the work we are doing there to be impracticable and that we should stop the dredging that is going on.

Not at all; this breastwork can be built while the dredging is going on. I wish the dredging to be proceeded with as rapidly as possible, but I urge that this breastwork be put in at the point of divergence. I think the chief engineer will understand what I mean.
Green Point (Beresford) breakwater, $10,000.

Might I ask the minister whether he intends to go on with this work. This amount has been voted and revoted since 1911 but nothing has been done. I do not blame the present Minister of Public Works for that, but it is very important the work should be done. If I were to trace the delay to its source I might find that the Minister of Marine had been the greatest sinner. I think it was he who told the late lamented Minister of Public Works, after representations had been made to him, which were not, however, justifiable, that the location was not a proper one. The lowest tenderer had already been awarded the contract, but he was later on advised that the plans and location might be changed. Reports have been made to the department recommending another site about one-quarter of a mile farther up than tne one first chosen by the engineer and recommended by myself and other gentle-266
men who know that district. The Minister of Marine knows I have made a study of these shores for the last forty years, and that it is of no consequence to me personally whether the location is a quarter of a mile further south or further north. I ask the minister to take the resident engineer into his confidence and to ask him whether he does not think the first site is the best.
I want to see this work undertaken at once.
I maintain that the first site is much more advantageous both for the present and the future, and extensions will probably be required in the course of time. Patronage probably had something to do with the selection of the new site. I am speaking with all the responsibility of a man who has the mandate of the electors of the county of Gloucester for the last fourteen or fifteen years when I say that the first site chosen is the more advantageous. The Minister of Marine and Fisheries knows I have as accurate information on this point as any of hie friends in Gloucester county. I would again urge the Minister of Public Works to take the resident engineer into his confidence, and to ask him whether the first site is not the more advantageous.
Edmonton-repairs to wharf and roadway, $2,800.

I wish to point out to the minister that there has been very strong representation made to the department in regard to the protection of the bank of the river at this point. The matter was under consideration of the department for a number of years and it has been also under the consideration of the city council. Has the minister anything in view at present except this very small amount in the Estimates'?

I do not recollect if there is any vote in the Supplementary Estimates, but I do recollect that during my visit to Edmonton I saw considerable reason why a certain amount of money should be expended for the protection of the bank of the river. I will give the matter consideration, because I appreciate the necessity of work being done at that point.

It is a very serious matter, and I think the position taken by the parties interested was that the parties owning the property immediately affected were prepared to urge that the city government become responsible for one-half of whatever expenditure would be required, on the understanding that the Dominion Government would be responsible for the other half. That was the position taken by the property owners in their recommendation



to the city council, but I cannot say what the view of the city council is. I can say that the matter is very urgent, and I am anxious that the Government should give it its best attention.
We will take the matter up with the city council.

This appropriation is
entirely inadequate for anything of that kind.

Oh, yes.
